readout_other: DESA; AHRS; MoCA; SAFTEE; C-SSRS (fMRI collected but not analysable)
direction_notes: Delusion experience scores (DESA) fell more after TUS than sham (p = 0.002); AHRS and MoCA did not differ. Neural direction was not assessed because the fMRI data were uninterpretable.
safety_notes: No serious adverse events; mild transient effects (fatigue, headache, GI discomfort, increased delusions or hallucinations) occurred after both TUS and sham, assessed with SAFTEE.

device.model: custom-made single-element fixed-depth 350 kHz transducer with plano-concave Delrin lens (STEMiNC SMD85T6R111 element)

timing.protocol_description: 0.5 ms rectangular pulses at a 100 Hz PRF (10 ms pulse repetition interval, 5% duty cycle); the 10-min protocol consisted of ten cycles of 30 s on and 30 s off. One TUS and one sham session one week apart.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The participants (N = 10) had a mean age of 37.5 years (SD = 9.8).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Participants were blindly randomized and underwent one active TUS and one sham session in random order, separated by one week.

flags.reason: Participants and all team members except the bioengineer were blinded, but the authors state the study should not be considered fully double-blinded and 6 of 10 guessed the condition correctly.

In situ values are derived by derating free-water output with a maximum skull transmission coefficient (upper bound) and a brain attenuation of 0.5 dB/cm/MHz over 6 cm; the abstract and results also give an estimated through-skull Ispta range of 0.29-0.4 W/cm2.
Ten cycles of 30 s on and 30 s off over 10 min; 30 s is the length of each uninterrupted train.
